title: Two supplied migration drafts
note: Why Moving Abroad Can Feel So Hard Substack Draft and Moving Abroad and Coping With Change. Same body; editorial framing, not independent research.

title: Change Examples
note: Thirteen pages. Selected, unverified online accounts and notes on Suzuki, Bonanno and Shankar; not a representative sample.

title: Refugee and migrant mental health
note: Conditions, access to services and community support across diverse migrant populations.

title: How to cope with loneliness
note: Read alongside the supplied nine-page Loneliness and Human Connection compilation of six interviews.

title: Social connection
note: Distinguishes social isolation, loneliness and relationship quality.

title: Change
note: Supplied 82-page SOLVED Change Guide and 451-page Change Solve transcript. Practical concepts; unsupported absolutes and sponsor claims excluded.

title: A systematic review of personality trait change through intervention
note: 207 studies, mainly clinical interventions. Changes in trait measures do not establish a universal self-help prescription.

title: Challenges to capture the Big Five personality traits in non-WEIRD populations
note: Measurement and administration challenges; not evidence that any population lacks personality traits.

title: Why change is so scary and how to unlock its potential
note: Reflection on capabilities, values and identity; also included in the supplied examples.

title: Why forcing positivity after trauma does not build resilience
note: Supplied Trauma Resilience transcript, especially flexibility at 31:27 and grief from 1:00:54.

title: Regulatory flexibility
note: Conceptual review of context sensitivity, strategy repertoire and feedback; migration examples are AGF adaptations.

title: Move your body grow your brain
note: Supplied Exercise Anxiety Brain transcript. Everyday versus clinical anxiety; enjoyable movement and small starts.

title: Guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behaviour
note: Adult activity guidance, including disability and chronic conditions. Figure 3 is illustrative scheduling.

title: Tackling your worries
note: Practical versus hypothetical worries and choosing a next action.

title: Post-traumatic stress disorder
note: Distress, symptoms and treatment; a move alone does not establish a diagnosis.

organisation: US National Institute of Mental Health
title: My Mental Health Do I Need Help
note: Symptoms and functioning. US crisis numbers are not generalised to other countries.

title: Doing What Matters in Times of Stress
note: Illustrated stress-management guide with multiple language editions.

title: The behaviour change wheel
note: COM-B: capability, opportunity and motivation.

title: Implementation intentions and goal achievement
note: Meta-analysis of plans specifying when, where and how to act.

title: How are habits formed
note: Habit automaticity developed at different rates. The study does not provide a timetable for migrant adjustment.
